author: Jimmy Parker
title: SPLC Gets Called Out Again
text:
Kirk Saw It Early
Charlie Kirk was not shy about the Southern Poverty Law Center. He said the group was not just wrong, but dangerous, because it kept slapping conservative and Christian groups with ugly labels while acting like it was some noble guardian of truth. That kind of branding is not debate. It is a pressure tactic, and it works the same way no matter how fancy the nonprofit letterhead looks. Kirk understood that if you cannot beat an idea, the left will often try to smear it first and call it a public service.
The Turning Point USA Fight
When SPLC put Turning Point USA on its so-called hate map, Kirk blasted the move as a cheap attempt to silence young conservatives. He said the group was lumping high school chapters in with the KKK and neo-Nazis, which is about as honest as a used-car ad written by a lawyer. Kirk argued that the goal was not dialogue, but surrender. Instead of debating the ideas, the left reached for the oldest trick in the book: call your opponent a racist, hope the crowd gets scared, and move on before anybody asks hard questions.
Why Conservatives Were Alarmed
Kirk also pointed to the real-world danger that can follow this kind of rhetoric. He cited the Family Research Council shooting as a grim reminder that political lists and smear campaigns are not harmless. Once activists and bureaucrats start treating believers, parents, and conservatives like enemies, the risk goes way up. That is why so many on the right have long viewed the SPLC as more of a political club than a civil-rights watchdog. When an organization keeps finding new reasons to target people who disagree with it, folks are right to ask who is really spreading hate.
His 2023 Warnings Still Matter
Kirk made the point plain in 2023 on social media, saying the SPLC was a hate group and warning that federal agencies were using that same style of rhetoric against Catholics who attend the Latin Mass. Whether you agree with every word he said or not, the larger issue is hard to miss. Institutions that should protect equal treatment sometimes borrow language from activists instead. That is a problem conservatives have been warning about for years, and Kirk was one of the loudest voices in that fight. He called it early, and now more people are seeing why.
The SPLC is a hate group.
